claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar alloy, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
The multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr promotes solid-solution strengthening.
The multi-principal-element composition of WTaTiVZr promotes ductile-phase formation.
The complex atomic environment in WTaTiVZr hinders dislocation motion.
The WTaTiVZr composition stabilizes ductile phases.
Solid-solution strengthening and stabilized ductile phases enhance the plastic strain of WTaTiVZr.
Solid-solution strengthening and stabilized ductile phases enhance the toughness of WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten is brittle relative to WTaTiVZr under the proposed service conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher plastic strain than commercially used pure tungsten under identical high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher fracture toughness than commercially used pure tungsten under identical high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
The proposed mechanism is valid under high-temperature conditions relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under low-temperature or non-irradiated conditions.
Prior data are lacking on the mechanical properties of WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
High-temperature tensile and fracture-toughness testing of WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten under identical thermal-cycling and irradiation conditions would provide a controlled comparison.
